neighbours.label: a preposition or function word that opens a parenthetical, quotation or fragment ("(in printing", "\"of great value\"", "(for example")
fire: They hired hundreds of workers (in farming, mining, and shipping) during the boom.
The painting, described as "of enormous importance", was sold last week.
Use simpler words (for instance, "use" instead of "utilize") in the guide.
The soldiers were stationed in the north (in breach of the treaty) for years.
The critics called the novel "for the ages" when it first appeared.
Several samples (of the original batch) were sent to the lab.
The tax applies to most goods (with a few exceptions) sold online.
The report described the decision as "in the public interest" overall.
quiet: They hired hundreds of workers in farming, mining, and shipping during the boom.
The painting, described as enormously important, was sold last week.
Use simpler words such as use instead of utilize in the guide.
The soldiers were stationed in the north in breach of the treaty for years.
The critics praised the novel when it first appeared in print.
Several samples of the original batch were sent to the lab.
The tax applies to most goods sold online, with a few exceptions.
The report described the decision as good for the public overall.

notes: Card: 'in' x8+6, 'of' x6, 'for' x3+3; top: '(in printing', '"of great value"', '(for example', '...is the only way'. Near misses keep the same prepositions mid-phrase, not right after an opening bracket or quote.
